summary: Non-monotonic rerank top-k after model alias rollout: similarity score drift
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that search results from the rerank endpoint are reordering unpredictably for identical queries after a model alias rollout earlier today. The behavior appears as: identical query -> sometimes returns expected top-k list, sometimes a different top-k that includes lower-relevance items.

Impact:
- LexiSearch customers observe flickering search results in production UI for ~5% of requests between 14:00-16:30 UTC.
- Business impact: Visible user confusion and several support tickets opened by LexiSearch customers.
- Customer requests an urgent mitigation and root-cause analysis.

Environment:
- prod-us-east cluster routing by alias "lexi-rerank-prod"
- Traffic distribution: canary rollout policy (10% new variant, 90% stable) with smart routing fallback enabled
- Affected endpoints: /v1/rerank and /v1/embeddings (embed generation upstream)

Observed behavior details:
- Non-monotonic top-k: rankings are not deterministic across requests that should be identical.
- Score drift: Same query + same document set yields different cosine/similarity scores depending on which model variant handled the embedding generation or rerank call.
- Time correlation: spikes coincide with alias routing changes and brief periods of mixed-variant handling for batched requests.

Desired outcome:
- Immediate mitigation to stop end-user visible flicker.
- Root cause and postmortem.
- Hardening checklist to prevent similar during future alias rollouts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer account lexicompany-342 on prod-us-east.
2) Send repeated identical rerank requests for query 'enterprise search scalability' with candidate set of 50 docs.
3) Observe top-10 across 50 repeated requests within a 10-minute window.
4) Note that ~5% of responses show different top-10 ordering and occasionally different items entering top-10.
5) Correlate with routing logs to see mixed handling across two model variants behind alias lexi-rerank-prod.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Model alias rollout introduced a variant with different embedding normalization (L2 scale) or changed tokenization leading to orientation/scale differences in embedding space.
Checked model-catalog: canary build includes small numerics change to final embedding layer (float32->float16 path) and a newer pre-normalization squeeze op. PR reference noted in related_github_prs.
Reproduced locally by calling both variants back-to-back: confirmed per-request differences in embed norms and subsequent cosine scores when reranker expects pre-normalized inputs.

Routing logs show some batched requests were split across both variants when batch size matched threshold; this caused candidate embeddings within a single rerank call to come from mixed variants in some traces.
Cache behavior: embedding cache keys do not include model-variant id (alias only); cache hits returned stable embeddings while mixed requests triggered fresh embed computation on different variant.
Potential contributing factor: Smart routing attempted to balance latency and cost by routing some embeds to canary variant; this led to mixed-variant candidate pools for the same rerank invocation.
comments: Olivia Chen (2026-03-10): Customer escalation opened after UX team reported flicker. Provided initial logs and sample request/response pairs.
Aisha Patel (2026-03-10): Acknowledged. Spun up live trace capture for affected customer org. Hypothesis: embedding normalization mismatch. Pinned alias to stable as immediate mitigation?

Benji Ramos (SRE, 2026-03-10): I can confirm routing mixed variants in some batched flows. Recommending temporary rollback of alias to stable variant and flush of embedding cache for lexicompany-342 namespace.
Aisha Patel (2026-03-10): Performed alias pin to stable variant at 2026-03-10T15:12:00Z for lexicompany-342. Also issued cache invalidation for embedding namespace. Waiting on customer verification.
LexiSearch Support (customer, 2026-03-10): Verified that flicker stopped after pin. Requests now consistently return stable top-k. Need root cause and safety guard for rollouts.
resolution: Workaround applied: pinned alias 'lexi-rerank-prod' back to stable variant and invalidated embedding cache for customer namespace. Customer confirmed flicker stopped. Next steps: rollback canary fleet globally, add model-variant id to embedding cache keys, and add a rollout gate that prevents mixing variant-derived embeddings within the same rerank invocation. Eng action items assigned to model-onboarding and routing teams.
